paragraphs.title: Renewed Mission and Journey to Nineveh

easy.explanation: Jonah 3:1 says, "And the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time."
easy.q: To whom did the word of the LORD come the second time?

easy.explanation: The LORD commanded Jonah, "Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city."
easy.q: To what city was Jonah commanded to go?

easy.explanation: Jonah arose and went unto Nineveh according to the word of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Jonah do after he was commanded to go to Nineveh?

medium.explanation: The LORD renewed Jonah's mission and commanded him again to go to Nineveh.
medium.q: What does the phrase "the second time" show about Jonah's mission?

answers: The great size or extent of the city
The number of people in the city
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Nineveh as a very large city.
medium.q: What does "three days' journey" most likely describe in this passage?

answers: Jonah acted according to the word of the LORD
medium.explanation: The passage says that Jonah went to Nineveh "according to the word of the LORD."
medium.q: What was the relationship between the LORD's command and Jonah's action?

answers: The mission was still in force
challenge.explanation: The renewed command shows that Jonah's mission to Nineveh still stood.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the LORD commanding Jonah to go to Nineveh again?

answers: It was a city of three days' journey
challenge.explanation: The description "a city of three days' journey" emphasizes Nineveh's great size.
challenge.q: Which detail especially emphasizes the greatness of Nineveh?

answers: He obeys and goes on the mission
challenge.explanation: Jonah arose and went to Nineveh as the LORD had commanded.
challenge.q: What is the main change in Jonah's behavior in these verses?

easy.explanation: Jonah proclaimed, "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown."
easy.q: How much time remained before Nineveh would be overthrown?

easy.explanation: Jonah began to enter into the city and cried out his warning there.
easy.q: Where did Jonah proclaim his warning?

answers: The king would change his clothing
easy.explanation: Jonah announced that Nineveh would be overthrown in forty days.
easy.q: What was the content of Jonah's proclamation?

answers: He entered the city to deliver the warning
He entered the city to sit in ashes
He entered the city to announce only a fast
medium.explanation: Jonah entered Nineveh and proclaimed the coming disaster.
medium.q: What was the connection between Jonah entering the city and his proclamation?

medium.explanation: In this context, "overthrown" refers to a severe destruction or overturning of the city.
medium.q: What does "overthrown" mean in Jonah's proclamation?

answers: The warning had no connection to their actions
The warning was only for the king
The warning pointed to the need for the city to change
medium.explanation: The warning created an opportunity for Nineveh to turn from its evil ways.
medium.q: How may the warning be related to the ways of the people of Nineveh?

answers: There was still time before the judgment
Jonah did not know the time
challenge.explanation: "Yet forty days" indicates that forty days remained before the announced overthrow.
challenge.q: What does the word "Yet" indicate in Jonah's proclamation?

answers: It was spoken only to the king
It left room for the city to change its ways
It described the size of the city
challenge.explanation: The warning led the people to believe God, fast, and turn from their evil ways.
challenge.q: Why can Jonah's proclamation be understood as a warning and not merely a prediction?

answers: Jonah leaves the city, then cries, and finally enters
Jonah announces a fast, and then Nineveh is rebuilt
Jonah enters the city, cries out, and announces forty days
challenge.explanation: The verse presents Jonah entering the city, crying out, and announcing the forty-day warning.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the verse?

paragraphs.title: The Response of the People and the King

easy.explanation: The passage says, "So the people of Nineveh believed God."
easy.q: How did the people of Nineveh respond to Jonah's proclamation?

easy.explanation: The people of Nineveh put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least.
easy.q: What did the people of Nineveh put on?

easy.explanation: The king removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
easy.q: Where did the king of Nineveh sit?

answers: People from every level of society responded
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that the response included everyone, from the greatest to the least.
medium.q: What does "from the greatest of them even to the least of them" show?

medium.explanation: Sackcloth was a rough garment associated with mourning, sorrow, and humility.
medium.q: What does "sackcloth" represent in this passage?

answers: The people responded, and the king joined them
The king opposed them, so they stopped
The king knew nothing about their response
medium.explanation: The people responded first, and the king also responded with mourning and humility.
medium.q: What was the relationship between the response of the people and the response of the king?

answers: He removed his robe and sat in ashes
challenge.explanation: Removing his royal robe and sitting in ashes showed mourning and submission.
challenge.q: Which detail especially expresses the king's humiliation and submission?

answers: The warning reached the rulers as well as the people
The king did not believe the warning
The people had not heard Jonah
challenge.explanation: The king's response shows that the message and its effects reached the leadership of Nineveh.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the king responded after the word came to him?

answers: He sat in ashes, removed his robe, and put on a crown
He removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes
He put on sackcloth, returned to his throne, and proclaimed a feast
challenge.explanation: This is the order given in Jonah 3:6.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of the king's actions?

easy.explanation: The decree was issued by the king and his nobles.
easy.q: Who issued the decree in Nineveh?

easy.explanation: The decree said, "Let neither man nor beast... taste any thing" and commanded them not to drink water.
easy.q: From what were both people and animals commanded to abstain?

answers: From their evil way and from the violence in their hands
easy.explanation: The decree called on everyone to turn from his evil way and from the violence in his hands.
easy.q: From what were the people commanded to turn?

answers: To show the broad extent of the fast
To drive the people out of the city
medium.explanation: Including the animals emphasizes that the decree applied throughout the whole city.
medium.q: Why does the decree include the animals?

medium.explanation: Here, violence refers to harmful, unjust, or oppressive actions.
medium.q: What does "violence" mean in the phrase "the violence that is in their hands"?

answers: They pray while also being required to correct their actions
They pray instead of changing their actions
They change their actions without turning to God
medium.explanation: The decree includes both calling upon God and turning from evil and violence.
medium.q: What is the connection between crying unto God and changing one's way?

answers: It was meant only for the king
It was comprehensive and included people and animals
It concerned only those who heard Jonah personally
challenge.explanation: The decree addressed the entire city and even included its animals.
challenge.q: What does the wording of the decree show about the extent of the required repentance?

answers: It expresses hope that God might turn from the judgment
It announces that the city was already destroyed
challenge.explanation: The words express hope that God would turn from His fierce anger and spare them.
challenge.q: Why does the decree say, "Who can tell"?

answers: Fast, cry unto God, and turn from evil and violence
challenge.explanation: The decree included fasting, calling upon God, and changing their conduct.
challenge.q: Which combination fully describes what the people were required to do?

paragraphs.title: The Decree Is Revoked After Their Changed Actions

answers: Their works and that they turned from their evil way
easy.explanation: The verse says that God saw their works and that they turned from their evil way.
easy.q: What did God see in the people of Nineveh?

answers: He brought the evil upon them
He did not bring the evil that He had said He would do
He sent them to another city
easy.explanation: God repented of the evil He had said He would do unto them, and He did it not.
easy.q: What did God do after the people of Nineveh repented?

answers: The changed actions of the people of Nineveh
The king's sitting in ashes alone
easy.explanation: The people turned from their evil way, and God withheld the announced judgment.
easy.q: What caused the judgment to be withheld?

answers: Verse 10 describes the result of the change required by the decree
Verse 10 gives an unrelated new decree
medium.explanation: After the people were commanded to turn from evil, God saw their change and withheld the judgment.
medium.q: What is the connection between verse 10 and the decree in verses 7–9?

answers: God turned back from the disaster He had planned to bring
medium.explanation: The phrase is explained by the statement that God did not bring the evil He had announced.
medium.q: What does "God repented of the evil" mean in this context?

answers: The people turned from their evil way
The king fled from the city
medium.explanation: The verse specifically says that they turned from their evil way.
medium.q: What explicit reason is given for God not bringing the evil?

answers: Actions do not affect the judgment
A genuine change in conduct leads to the judgment being withheld
Only the king's position determines the outcome
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the people's changed actions with God's decision not to bring the judgment.
challenge.q: What principle of cause and effect appears at the end of the chapter?

answers: Repentance includes a genuine change from an evil way
An outward response is more important than changed actions
challenge.explanation: God saw not only their fasting and sackcloth, but also that they turned from their evil way.
challenge.q: What is the difference between an outward response and repentance as shown here?

answers: Proclamation, belief and repentance, then the judgment is withheld
The judgment is withheld, then the proclamation, and finally repentance
Proclamation, destruction of the city, then repentance
challenge.explanation: Jonah proclaimed the warning, Nineveh believed and changed its ways, and God did not bring the announced evil.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly summarizes Jonah chapter 3?
